title: Why Do We Have Seasons? | Space Atlas
description: Earth is closest to the Sun in Northern winter. Seasons come from axial tilt, not distance — drag through an orbit to see why.
ogDescription: Earth's axis stays pointed the same direction all year — drag through an orbit and watch why that alone causes summer and winter.
jsonldDescription: An interactive 3D model of Earth's fixed axial tilt through a full orbit, showing that seasons are caused by tilt rather than distance from the Sun.
